questions.question: If two forces of equal size are acting on a box in opposite directions, what can we say about these forces?
options: They are balanced.
They are unbalanced.
They create a turning effect.
They are contact forces.

questions.question: An object has a force of 10 N pushing it to the right and a force of 4 N pulling it to the left. What is the resultant force acting on the object?
options: 14 N to the right
6 N to the right
14 N to the left
6 N to the left

questions.question: When the forces acting on a moving car are balanced, what happens to the car's speed?
options: The speed increases.
The speed decreases.
There is no change in speed.
The car immediately stops.

questions.question: If a toy boat has a 5 N force pushing it east and a 2 N force pushing it west, in which direction will the resultant force act?
options: West, because it has the smaller force
East, because it has the bigger force
North, because the forces cancel out
South, because of gravity

questions.question: How does the size of the resultant force acting on an object affect its change in speed?
options: The greater the resultant force, the greater or faster the change in speed.
The greater the resultant force, the slower the change in speed.
The size of the resultant force has no effect on the change in speed.
A greater resultant force prevents any change in speed.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the force of friction?
options: A force that pulls objects towards the Earth
The force of one surface gripping or rubbing on another
The force that pushes things up in water
A force that only acts in a vacuum

questions.question: What is the primary reason for adding a lubricant, like oil, between two moving metal surfaces?
options: To increase the weight of the metal parts
To reduce the friction between the surfaces
To make the surfaces rougher
To increase the contact area

questions.question: Which scientific instrument is used to measure the size of a force?
options: A thermometer
A newton meter
A measuring cylinder
A weighing balance

questions.question: What is the standard scientific unit used to measure force?
options: Kilograms (kg)
Newtons (N)
Joules (J)
Metres (m)

questions.question: What must you do to a newton meter before starting an experiment if no forces are acting on it?
options: Adjust it so that it reads zero
Set it to its maximum scale reading
Shake it to loosen the internal spring
Heat it up to calibrate it

questions.question: In an experiment investigating friction, you test different materials (wood, plastic, rubber, metal). What type of chart should you use to display your results?
options: A line graph
A scatter graph
A bar chart
A pie chart only

questions.question: To make an investigation a fair test, how many variables should we change?
options: Only the variable we are testing
At least two variables
All of the variables
None of the variables

questions.question: During a fair test, what must be done to all the variables that we are not testing?
options: They must be changed randomly.
They must be kept the same for every measurement.
They must be ignored completely.
They must be increased gradually.

questions.question: Which of the following describes contact forces?
options: They only act when objects are touching.
They can act with or without objects touching.
They only act in outer space.
They only act when objects are moving away from each other.

questions.question: What is a key characteristic of non-contact forces?
options: They can only act when objects are rubbing together.
They can act with or without the objects touching.
They are only found inside magnetic materials.
They require a lubricant to work.

questions.question: What is drag?
options: A non-contact force that pulls objects towards the ground
A contact force that pushes against objects moving through liquids or gases
The force that causes objects to speed up in a vacuum
A force that only acts when two solid surfaces rub together

questions.question: In physics diagrams, what do force arrows represent?
options: The speed of a moving object
The direction of a force
The time it takes for a force to act
The distance an object has travelled

questions.question: How is the size of a force represented when drawing force arrows?
options: By the colour of the arrow
By the length of the arrow
By the width of the arrowhead
By the angle of the arrow

questions.question: Why does a heavy loaded lorry require a much greater braking distance than a light car travelling at the same speed?
options: The motion of heavier objects is harder to stop.
Heavier objects experience less air resistance.
Heavier objects are not affected by gravity.
The motion of heavier objects is easier to stop.

questions.question: In science, what is a force?
options: A type of energy store
A push or a pull
The speed of an object
The temperature of a substance
